questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I had studied and lived here before so I knew it was exactly here I wanted to go.
That it was it in city and thus had access to a lot of leisure activities and opportunities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: While I met great people and had unique experiences, the university itself did lack in providing assistance and guidance to us exchange students, if we wanted to get involved with anything or meet other students it was mostly up to us to do so. It did feel empthy from the university´s side.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A lot of written information such as guide leaflets and complete folders were provided, thus it was fairly easy to get the practical things done.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The staff at the dormitory were very helpful and explained a lot upon arrival. They were very helpful through the whole stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
The orientation was lackluster, it was poorly prepared and it felt like 5 minutes worth of information followed by questions and information about small insignificant things.
The orientation speech should provide a lot more information as the students arrive in a completely different environment with usually no prior knowledge or experience.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived at the university dorm although it was off campus, since the application was through the exchange university it was easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend living in the university dormitories, you make friends and have great experiences from day one, even as an introvert it was great to have friendly housemates to talk to, experience the country with and we helped each other a lot.
Be prepared for house rules and sometimes noise though, as several people living together requires some rules, for example about cleaning. Some people also can have different noise levels etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was great and very spacious flat with a big kitchen and balcony with a view. The rooms were small so do not bring too much stuff, some people brough two suitcases worth of stuff (bad idea).
The staff are helpful and kind and make sure everything is clean. The walk to the train station was only 5 minutes so very convenient. The commute to campuses were 40-60 minutes door to door so be prepared for travel time if living off campus.
Event were happening such as language exchange, food nights etc if that is interesting to you.
I mostly hung out with my housemates and experienced the city, so a great recommendation from me even if you do not want bigger gatherings.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The application and registration processes can be very compehensive, be prepared for a lot of paper work, documents to get and time, it took several months for the whole process with multiple rounds of paper work that had to be provided. The whole process could definitely be streamlined and simplified in my opinion.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Multiple rounds of documents and applications that had to be sent by set deadlines.
A lot of paper work to be filled out and sent. A guide for application got provided so we knew what we had to get, but there were many steps in the whole process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to contact both our home universtiy, and the host university did also provide assistance through email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was very smooth and easy, I got all the classes I wanted and I believe everyone did too. Since most of the courses are close to the previous semester, we get a clear idea of what courses will be provided.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to both provide our home university as well as the host university with seperate applications and documents, prepare documents early.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had great teachers from multiple countries and they were very kind and positive, they managed to encourage us to participate.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The courses were about the same and provided us with a great about of knowledge.
More smaller written assignments instead of a big one.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It was a mix depending on the teacher. Some Americans and Canadians were very positive and inviting with a great deal of participation from the class, they provided a safe and open classroom where we were not affraid of failing which gave us confidence in experimenting.

Other teachers were more of the formal teacher speaker - student listen kind of style. They were always open and encouraging to questions and provided a ton of information with visual aids such as slideshows and videos etc.

I really liked that we had weekly small written assignments instead of one big one we have at out home university.
I could experiement with small assignements and dared to try something new. It improved my writing as we did it very often but in bite sized amounts, It also helped me to get an assignment started quicker as we got more practice in doing so.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.answer:
Global Studies in English (Fall Winter)

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Japanese Law (Spring Summer)
Introduction to Comparative Law (Spring Summer)
UC Frontier Science I (Spring Summer)
International Exchange Lecture on Nanoscience and Nanoengineering A (Spring Summer)
Islamic Family Law (Spring Summer)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Global Studies in English (Fall Winter)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Higher cost of transportation between cities.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Fruit and meat was more expensive.
Eating out was cheaper than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were opportunities but it was not as well introduced to us.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kind of sports clubs such as swimming and archery and cultural clubs such as dance and music.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depends on your hobbies and personality, but seeking out a school club in an area you are interested in could be a great way to meet the local students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Explore the city both with people but also alone. Nearby cities are also worth visiting.
Take your time and really enjoy it when doing things insead of rushing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The local culture is very different, probably even more different than one can image, so be prepared to be very open minded and positive.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Activities and cubs are great but local roommates should also be living there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Reading the air and following social cues. It is important to pay attention to small gestures and how people say things. People are not as direct or confrontational as Danes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The respect of other people and their surroundings, this makes for pleasant, quiet and safe living.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Study up on the culture as in how people interact and their mindsets, this will help you avoid bad or awkward situations, I have seen many people do this.
Be prepared to seek out things yourself, this can be scary but very rewarding
The campus provide a great deal of facilities and opportunities.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The host university had tree campuses, so have this in mind when choosing classes as they will be spread out and it takes up to an hour to travel between them. Try therefore to group classes on the same campus together.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Meeting great housemates and going out to drink and eat with them.
Learning more about myself as I can mirror myself in other people and how they are.
Having classes with a very different style than our home university, I really appriciated experiencing other approaches.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to everything being foreign and different, while it is great, it can be a shock initially.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
It is definitely worth it. There are so many great things to experience and see and people to meet.
The different classroom styles and teachers give you a different perspective and thus you become a better student.
Be prepared for a shock or hardship in the beginning but do not give up, you will adjust way quicker than you think and you will have the time of your life before you know it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
